issues.description: Identity-based GKE detection complects naming convention with semantic intent
issues.detail: Name-prefix matching ('gke-') is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: it conflates a string identity with the fact 'this VM is managed by GKE.' Users can name any VM gke-foo and bypass the check; real GKE node-pool name templates can change. The actual fact lives in instance labels/metadata (goog-gke-node, kube-labels). Carry that fact as data, not as a substring guess.

issues.description: Check name and metadata disagree with implementation's tri-state semantics
issues.detail: The check is named single_network_interface and the metadata describes PASS/FAIL only, but the code emits a third state (MANUAL) and the PR description says PASS/FAIL. Three concerns are complected: 'how many NICs', 'is this GKE', 'what status to report'. Make the value (nic_count) and the policy (what statuses mean) separable, and align metadata + name + code on one story.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model drops the data that makes the finding actionable
issues.detail: The interface is modeled as {name, network, subnetwork} but the real facts that distinguish a bridge from a benign multi-NIC (accessConfigs/natIP, network URL, alias IP ranges, stack type) are discarded at parse time. The check then can't ask the interesting question: 'do these NICs cross trust boundaries?' Keep the value richer; the check becomes a pure function over it.

issues.description: Tests assert serialized prose strings, complecting test with message wording
issues.detail: Six tests pin exact status_extended strings. That couples test outcomes to a presentation concern (the sentence) rather than to the fact under test (count, classification, instance id). A wording tweak breaks unrelated tests. Assert the value (status, count, names list) and let the message be formatted separately.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch is a silent PASS that hides a contradiction
issues.detail: If interface_count == 0 the report stays PASS with a 'has no network interfaces' message. That is not a single interface; it is an impossible-for-a-running-VM state worth surfacing as MANUAL or INFO rather than asserting compliance. The 'easy' default (status starts at PASS) made the unusual case invisible.

issues.description: CHANGELOG entry contradicts the security framing
issues.detail: The PR title and description are about detecting VMs with multiple NICs (a risk signal). The CHANGELOG line reads as 'single_network_interface check', which describes the desired state rather than what the check finds. Small thing, but the naming chose 'easy' (mirrors the file name) over 'simple' (says what the check is about). Decide if the artifact is named for the violation or the desideratum, and be consistent across metadata, title, and changelog.

review.summary: The check answers a useful question but the design complects several concerns that should be separable: GKE-ness inferred from a name prefix instead of carried as data; nic-count policy mixed with presentation strings; the NetworkInterface value model strips exactly the fields (accessConfigs, alias ranges, network URL) that would let the check distinguish a real cross-boundary bridge from a benign dual-NIC. The tri-state MANUAL branch also disagrees with the metadata and PR description (PASS/FAIL), which is the kind of EASY-NOT-SIMPLE drift that bites later. Decompose: a richer NetworkInterface value, a pure classifier (count + gke-managed + crosses-networks), and a separate formatter for status_extended. Then the tests assert facts, not sentences, and the check can grow without a rewrite. Decision label: COMPLECTED with INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY around identity-as-string.
